entities.name: Philipp von Cobenzl
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Philipp von Cobenzl (1683-1810) was a statesman of the Habsburg monarchy and the Austrian Empire.

 As the Austrian Envoy to France from 1797 to 1803, he played a crucial role in negotiating the Treaty of Pressburg, which forced Napoleon to relinquish his Austrian territories.

 As a diplomat, von Cobenzl was instrumental in securing the Austrian alliance with Britain during the French Revolutionary Wars, which ultimately contributed to the defeat of Napoleon at the Battle of Waterloo in 1815.

 His legacy in Austrian history is marked by his efforts to modernize the Habsburg administration and promote cultural exchange between Austria and other European nations.

 The phrase ' Die Welt ist ein Theater, und wir nur Schauspieler' ('The world is a theatre, and we are only actors'), attributed to von Cobenzl, reflects his pragmatic understanding of the interconnectedness of politics and culture.
